newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up on Monday due to two new domestic A share issues on the Shanghai stock exchange on Monday and Tuesday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 13.91 percent from 12.14 percent last Friday.
The earliest-maturing three-day contract soared to 35.0 percent from 5.6 percent.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 12.81 million lots from 8.3 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said big institutions borrowed heavily on the repo market on Monday due to the two new A share issues.
"The new issues boosted fund demand on the repo market, pushing up the repo rates, especially those for the early-maturing contracts," said one trader.
"The speed to issue new A shares has become quicker and quicker in the past few weeks, which will surely support the repo rates in the short term," he added.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down across the board on Monday on the active A share markets, which are attracting liquidity from the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell slightly to 119.10 yuan from 119.12 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 939,356 lots from 1.02 million lots.
Traders said they believed the spot prices would around the curent level in the next few days.
